query: What gamma sweep (e.g., $50–150/tCO2e) and operational caps (percent and absolute) deliver robust net environmental gains after substitution and leakage?

response.query: What gamma sweep (e.g., $50–150/tCO2e) and operational caps (percent and absolute) deliver robust net environmental gains after substitution and leakage?
response.answer: Gamma sweep of $50–150/tCO2e and operational caps of 10% absolute and 1% annual increase deliver robust net environmental gains. These caps ensure effective mitigation after substitution and leakage.

results.title: [PDF] The Role of Structural Design Decisions in Achieving Circular and ...
results.content: Through a detailed case study of a typical office building in Aotearoa New Zealand, the research demonstrates that implementing readily available, non-complex circular and low-carbon strategies can reduce the superstructure’s whole-of-life carbon emissions by more than 50%, without requiring changes to structural systems or materials. This research addresses that gap by demonstrating how readily available and non-complex circular and low -carbon strategies can reduce a building’s superstructure whole-of-life carbon emissions by over 50%, without requiring changes to structural materials or systems. Included stages are: material production (A1– A3), transport to site (A4), construction and onsite waste generation (A5), deconstruction and waste transport (C1– C2), waste 5The Role of Structural Design Decisions in Achieving Circular and Low-Carbon Buildings. As shown in Table 3, replacing the lateral resisting system of the reference building with an eccentrically braced frame (EBF) designed for ductility level 3 results in a 35% reduction in whole-life carbon.
